name: Log gym sets from Telegram to Notion

nodes.name: Load today's sets
nodes.notes: A workout day runs from 4 AM to 4 AM, so a late session after midnight stays on the same date. Empty on the first set of the day; Build context handles that.

nodes.name: Build context
nodes.notes: Exercise names Gemini should match against, plus what has been logged so far today.

assignments.name: text
assignments.value: ={{ String($json.transcriptFile || $('Transcribe an audio').first().json.text || $('Transcribe an audio').first().json.transcription || $('Transcribe an audio').first().json.data?.text || $('Transcribe an audio').first().json.data?.transcription || '').trim() }}

nodes.name: Plan changes
nodes.notes: Decides what to store (new sets, undo or correction), numbers the sets, and builds today's date toggle for Notion from the final list of sets: one toggle per exercise holding a Set / Reps / Weight table. Also builds the Telegram reply.

nodes.name: Find day block
nodes.notes: Reads the top of the Workout Log page to find the callout and, if it exists, the toggle for today.

nodes.name: Delete old day block
nodes.notes: Today's toggle is rebuilt from scratch on every message, so it always matches the stored sets.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ children: [{ object: 'block', type: 'heading_2', heading_2: { rich_text: [{ type: 'text', text: { content: $('Plan changes').first().json.dayTitle } }], is_toggleable: true } }], position: $('Find day block').first().json.results.some(block => block.type === 'callout') ? { type: 'after_block', after_block: { id: $('Find day block').first().json.results.find(block => block.type === 'callout').id } } : { type: 'start' } }) }}

nodes.name: Create day block
nodes.notes: Adds the date toggle right under the callout so the newest day is on top. Its content is added by the next node because Notion allows only two levels of nesting per request.

options.systemMessage:
You read a short note a gym-goer sent between sets (usually a transcribed voice note, spoken casually with no fixed format) and return ONLY a JSON object, no prose.

Schema:
{
  "intent": "log_sets" | "undo_last" | "correct_last" | "summary" | "unclear",
  "day_focus": "Chest" | "Back" | "Shoulders" | "Biceps" | "Triceps" | "Legs" | "Core" | "Cardio" | "Full Body" | null,
  "sets": [ { "exercise": string, "muscle_group": string, "reps": number, "weight": number, "unit": "kg" | "lb" } ],
  "correction": { "reps": number | null, "weight": number | null, "unit": "kg" | "lb" | null } | null,
  "question": string | null
}

Rules:
- Answering your question: when an earlier note is waiting for an answer and the new message answers your question (for example it only gives the missing reps or weights), combine the earlier note and the new message into one complete answer. Earlier "leg press four sets of 10 kg 12 kg 15 kg 13 kg" plus now "eleven, twelve, eleven, twelve" means four Leg Press sets: 11x10, 12x12, 11x15, 12x13. Pair the values in the order they were said. If the new message is a new, complete note instead, ignore the earlier one.
- log_sets: the note reports one or more sets. Add one entry to "sets" per set performed. "3 sets of 10 at 20" is three identical entries. "12 at 20, then 10 at 22" is two entries.
- Every set needs a rep count and a weight that the user actually said (or clearly implied with "same" or "3 sets of 10 at 20"). Numbers like "first", "second", "set 1", "1", "2" placed before a value are usually set numbers, not reps. If you cannot tell which number is the reps and which is the weight for any set, do NOT guess: return intent "unclear" and ask one short question, for example "How many reps did you do in each set?".
- exercise: use the exact name from Known exercises whenever it matches, including aliases and speech-to-text mistakes (for example "jumble row" is Dumbbell Row). Only use a new name (Title Case, standard gym name) when nothing matches, and then set muscle_group from the allowed day_focus values.
- If the note names no exercise ("next set", "same again", "10 at 50"), use the Last exercise logged.
- Ignore spoken set numbers such as "second set"; the system numbers sets itself.
- unit is kg unless the user says pounds or lbs. Bodyweight moves with no weight use 0.
- day_focus: set it only when the user names the day ("today is chest day", "leg day"). "Chess day" means Chest.
- undo_last: "undo", "delete that", "remove the last set".
- correct_last: the user fixes the previous set ("that was 25 not 22.5", "actually 8 reps"). Fill only the changed fields in correction.
- summary: "summary", "what did I do today", "how many sets".
- unclear: anything else, or numbers you cannot tie to an exercise. Put a short question for the user in "question".

nodes.name: Extract workout data
nodes.notes: ChatGPT reads the note and returns JSON (intent, sets, correction). The chat model is forced to JSON output; Plan changes parses it and falls back to a help reply if it is not valid.

nodes.name: Load pending question
nodes.notes: The question the bot asked in its last reply, if it is still waiting for an answer. Empty when nothing is pending.

nodes.name: Remember open question
nodes.notes: Saves the note and question when the bot had to ask something, so the next reply can complete it. Clears it after any other reply.

nodes.name: Read transcript file
nodes.notes: deAPI hands back the transcript as a file in binary 'data'. This turns it into text. If deAPI ever returns the text inline instead, this step errors softly and Use voice transcript falls back to the JSON fields.
